full_name: AMSGrad: A New Exponential Moving Average Variant
source_reference: Reddi, Kale, and Kumar, ICLR 2018, On the Convergence of Adam and Beyond (Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4)

problem.description: Online convex optimization in the full-information feedback setting; the algorithm chooses x_t in the feasible set, observes f_t, and regret is measured against the best fixed point in the feasible set.

variable_space.math: x_t \in \mathcal{F}, \text{ where } \mathcal{F}\in \mathbb{R}^d \text{ is the feasible set of points}

assumptions.name: Online_convex_functions
assumptions.math: \text{The first inequality is due to convexity of function } f_t.
assumptions.ref: Appendix D, immediately after Eq. (16), p.16

assumptions.name: Convex_feasible_set
assumptions.math: For any Q\in S_+^d \text{ and convex feasible set } \mathcal{F}\subset\mathbb{R}^d, \text{ suppose } u_1=\min_{x\in\mathcal{F}}\|Q^{1/2}(x-z_1)\| \text{ and } u_2=\min_{x\in\mathcal{F}}\|Q^{1/2}(x-z_2)\|

assumptions.name: Bounded_gradients
assumptions.math: \|\nabla f_t(x)\|_\infty \le G_\infty \text{ for all } t\in[T] \text{ and } x\in\mathcal{F}

output.description: Algorithm 2 has no printed output line; it generates the online prediction sequence x_t through the displayed projected-update loop.

main_theorem.statement_math:
Let \{x_t\} and \{v_t\} be the sequences obtained from Algorithm 2, \alpha_t=\alpha/\sqrt{t}, \beta_1=\beta_{11}, \beta_{1t}\le\beta_1 for all t\in[T] and \gamma=\beta_1/\sqrt{\beta_2}<1. Assume that \mathcal{F} has bounded diameter D_\infty and \|\nabla f_t(x)\|_\infty\le G_\infty for all t\in[T] and x\in\mathcal{F}. For x_t generated using the AMSGRAD (Algorithm 2), we have the following bound on the regret
\[
R_T\le \frac{D_\infty^2\sqrt{T}}{\alpha(1-\beta_1)}\sum_{i=1}^d \hat v_{T,i}^{1/2}+\frac{D_\infty^2}{2(1-\beta_1)}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^d \frac{\beta_{1t}\hat v_{t,i}^{1/2}}{\alpha_t}+\frac{\alpha\sqrt{1+\log T}}{(1-\beta_1)^2(1-\gamma)\sqrt{1-\beta_2}}\sum_{i=1}^d\|g_{1:T,i}\|_2.
\]
main_theorem.rate: Data-dependent regret bound; with the decreasing momentum schedules discussed after Theorem 4, the regret is O(sqrt(T)) up to coordinate-adaptive gradient-history terms.
main_theorem.measure: Online regret R_T of AMSGrad against the best fixed point in the feasible set.

\]
